evidence.note: Builds reference.py oracle, sets TodoWrite milestones, then writes/runs test_correctness.py — an explicit reference stage with a done-check before any performance work.
Debugs kernel against the reference until correctness passes, and only then writes bench.py and runs the first benchmark: a clean correctness-then-latency stage boundary.

Optimization stage itself decomposed per kernel component (proj_gate, triton bmm, ln_gate_to_out), each tuned and then immediately re-tested+benched — per-milestone exit checks localizing regressions.
Strict allclose/failing-element checks catch fast-but-wrong precision changes (bf16 vs fp32 bmm out) and trigger reverts — checks that prevent fast-but-wrong regressions during tuning.

Full 10-shape/multi-seed strict correctness sweeps exist but arrive late and interleaved with optimization rather than as a single pre-optimization gate; hardest-case (Cauchy/large-N) risk-first sequencing is not distinctly shown.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it built an independent reference oracle, gated a correct kernel against it before touching latency, and decomposed the optimization stage into per-component milestones each with test+bench exit checks that repeatedly caught and reverted fast-but-wrong precision regressions (matching the level-8 and part of the level-10 descriptors). It falls short of a full 10 because the comprehensive domain/Cauchy correctness sweep was interleaved into the optimization phase rather than serving as a frozen pre-optimization gate, and there is no clear risk-first sequencing of the hardest cases. This places observed behavior solidly at 8.
